summary.goal: Process-signal pipeline orchestrating all stages: Greenhouse gate (Tier 0) then Tier 1 rules then Tier 2 ML then Tier 3 LLM extraction then Score then Near dedup then Cluster then Store then SSE broadcast. Atomic semantics: no partial signals. Does NOT handle chunking (that is pre-pipeline in ingest-document worker).

acceptance_criteria.description: Pipeline executes stages in order: Tier 0 -> Tier 1 -> Tier 2 -> Tier 3 extract -> Score -> Near dedup -> Cluster -> Store -> SSE
A signal that passes all stages is fully stored with extraction, scores, and cluster assignment
A signal that fails any stage does not produce a partial record in storage
On unrecoverable failure, the job enters dead letter queue after BullMQ retry exhaustion
Each pipeline stage records a StepProvenance entry tracking stage name, duration, and outcome
SSE signal:new event is broadcast on successful pipeline completion
Pipeline integrates with BullMQ process-signal worker as the job processor

steps.title: Define ProcessSignalContext type
steps.description: Create the ProcessSignalContext type that flows through the pipeline carrying accumulated state: raw signal data, greenhouse_id, filter results, extraction result, scoring result, cluster assignment, dedup result, and provenance trail (StepProvenance[]). Each stage reads what it needs and appends its output. Define StepProvenance type with stage_name, started_at, completed_at, outcome (passed/filtered/failed), and optional reason.

steps.title: Implement pipeline orchestrator
steps.description: Build processSignal(rawSignal, greenhouseId, dependencies) as the main pipeline function. Wire all stages in sequence: (1) Greenhouse gate - verify signal matches Greenhouse keyword filters, (2) Tier 1 - run rule registry filter, (3) Tier 2 - run ML classification, (4) Tier 3 - run Sonnet extraction, (5) Score - compute multi-factor score, (6) Near dedup - check for near duplicates post-extraction, (7) Cluster - assign to cluster via Haiku, (8) Store - persist complete signal, (9) SSE - broadcast signal:new. Each stage receives and returns ProcessSignalContext.

steps.title: Add atomic success-or-dead-letter semantics
steps.description: Ensure pipeline atomicity: if any stage after Tier 0/1/2 filtering throws, no partial signal is stored. Use a transactional approach — only call storage.insertSignal() after all processing stages complete successfully. Filter rejections (Tiers 0/1/2) are clean exits (not errors) that record provenance but do not store the signal. Unhandled errors propagate to BullMQ for retry/dead-letter handling.

steps.title: Implement provenance tracking per stage
steps.description: Wrap each pipeline stage with provenance recording. Before each stage, record started_at. After each stage, record completed_at and outcome. On filter rejection, record outcome 'filtered' with reason. On error, record outcome 'failed' with error message. Store the complete StepProvenance[] array with the signal for full pipeline audit trail. Provenance is stored even for filtered signals (in a separate filtered_signals table or log).

steps.title: Add SSE broadcast on completion
steps.description: After successful signal storage, call sseBroadcaster.emit('signal:new', { signal_id, greenhouse_id, cluster_id, score }) to notify connected clients. On cluster assignment to a new cluster, also emit 'cluster:new'. On assignment to existing cluster, emit 'cluster:updated' with updated signal count. SSE emission is the final pipeline step and its failure should not roll back the stored signal.

steps.title: Integrate with BullMQ process-signal worker
steps.description: Create the BullMQ worker for the 'process-signal' queue that invokes processSignal() for each job. Job data contains raw signal content, source metadata, and greenhouse_id. Configure worker concurrency, retry policy (exponential backoff, max 3 retries), and dead letter queue. On job failure after max retries, move to dead letter with full error context and provenance trail.
